<a id="export-families"></a>

### Export families

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** get the families out of this model and into a folder.

Saves loadable families out of the open project, each as its own file in a folder. How you recover a family from a model somebody sent, and how a whole project's family set goes into a library in one pass. **IT WORKS BECAUSE EDITING A FAMILY HANDS BACK A DOCUMENT WITH NO WINDOW.** The open project cannot be saved from here - that restriction is about the document somebody is looking at - but a family opened for editing is a separate background document, and one with no window saves normally. That is the whole mechanism, and it is why this changes nothing in the project. **EVERY FAMILY DOCUMENT IS CLOSED AGAIN, WHETHER OR NOT IT SAVED.** Leaving them open is what turns a run over four hundred families into a Revit that has to be restarted. The close happens on the failure path too. **THE FILE NAME IS THE FAMILY NAME WITH WHAT WINDOWS REFUSES TAKEN OUT.** A family called *300 x 150 / 45deg* is legal in Revit and not on a disk, and the save throws on it. Names are cleaned, and the cleaned name is reported next to the original so two families that clean to the same name are visible rather than one quietly overwriting the other. **IT IS A PUBLISH, NOT A MODIFY.** Nothing in the model changes; files appear outside it. That is a higher risk than changing an element, because what leaves the model is no longer under its control. **SINCE VERSION 2 IT RUNS WITH NO TRANSACTION GROUP OPEN IN THE PROJECT (D-192).** Revit opens a family for editing only while no transaction is open in the project, and version 1 ran inside Heron's group - so every family was refused (rows 21, 5b-1407, 5b-1411). Heron counts the project before and after, and refuses loudly if it moved. Not yet run in Revit that way (NEEDS-CHECKING Group OX). ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and must not: each family is a separate document, and a transaction in the project would not cover them anyway.

<a id="export-model-to-ifc"></a>

### Export model to IFC

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** export this model to an IFC file for issue.

Exports the model to a single IFC file, at a named schema version, optionally narrowed to one discipline or one storey. **The schema version is the deliverable, and getting it wrong is silent.** A recipient expecting IFC 2x3 and handed IFC 4 opens the file, sees geometry, and finds properties missing or renamed - it looks like a bad model rather than a wrong format. So the version is required from the request and never defaulted. **Scope is a choice and it is not defaulted** - the whole model, or one slice of it. See the note below the contract for how that is expressed and why it matters to a submission. **Base quantities are asked for explicitly** because a quantity take-off downstream needs them and they are off by default, so an IFC that looks complete arrives with no volumes or areas in it.

| **You get** | created |

<a id="export-view-image"></a>

### Export view image

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-20 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** save these views out as pictures.

Writes views and sheets out as PNG, JPG, TIFF, BMP or TGA images at a chosen width or DPI - the "send them a picture of this" job, done at a real resolution instead of a screenshot of whatever the screen happened to show. **It writes files onto a disk, which is why it is PUBLISH and not MODIFY.** An export leaves the model alone and puts something where other people can find it, and that is a higher bar than changing a duct. The folder is reported back because somebody has to be told where their drawings went. **Revit names the files itself and this does not pretend otherwise.** The prefix given is a stem; Revit appends the view type and the view name to it. So the filenames are never predicted: the folder is read afterwards and the files this run wrote are listed from it, with their pixel sizes. **A view that cannot be printed is not exported, and is named.** Templates, and some view types, cannot go to an image at all. Silently dropping them gives a folder with fewer files than views and nothing saying which are missing. **No transaction, and that is not an oversight.** An export reads the model and writes a file; it changes nothing to undo.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model and writes files outside it (`PUBLISH`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **views** - comma separated, resolved BY NAME in Revit; a name matching twice is refused<br>**folder** - text<br>**file prefix** - text<br>**pixel width** - a whole number - digits only - 250, not 250mm; optional, left out means *0*<br>**file type** - text; optional, left out means *png*<br>**dpi** - text; optional, left out means *keep* |
| **You get** | exported, files written, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2020 |
| **Capability** | `EXPORT_VIEW_IMAGE` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes and Publish** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"save these views as pictures"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

Other ways to ask: *"export a png of this sheet"* · *"send them an image of the plan"*

<a id="export-views-to-dwg"></a>

### Export views to DWG

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** export these views or sheets to DWG files in this folder.

Exports a set of views or sheets to DWG, one file each, into a folder. **The first fragment that writes outside the model, and the risk is a different shape.** Every other write here is undoable in Revit. This one puts files on a disk, and a name that matches an existing file OVERWRITES it with no undo and no warning. So the folder is checked, and files that would be overwritten are reported rather than quietly replaced. **The export setup comes from the project, not from defaults.** Layer mapping, line weights and text handling live in a named DWG export setup that the office has agreed; exporting with Revit's out-of-the-box options produces a file that opens fine and fails the recipient's CAD standard. The setup is asked for by name and its absence is a refusal, not a fallback.

<a id="export-views-to-fbx"></a>

### Export views to FBX

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-11 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** export the 3d view for the visualisation people.

Exports 3D views to FBX - the handover format for visualisation and coordination software that will not take a Revit file. **FBX TAKES 3D VIEWS AND NOTHING ELSE.** A plan, a section or a sheet in the list is rejected by Revit with an error about the export rather than about the view, so they are separated here and named. That is the commonest way this fails and it looks like the export itself is broken. **WHAT THE VIEW SHOWS IS WHAT THE FILE CONTAINS.** An FBX carries the view's visibility exactly: a hidden category, a section box, a view filter, a workset switched off - all of it travels. Exporting the wrong 3D view sends somebody a model with the services missing, and nothing in the file says so. Check the view before, not the file after. **IT READS THE MODEL AND CHANGES NOTHING, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS NO TRANSACTION.** It is still a PUBLISH: what leaves the model is no longer under its control, and that is a higher risk than changing an element. ASSUMES NOTHING ABOUT TRANSACTIONS - it opens none and must not.

<a id="list-export-setups"></a>

### List export setups

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** the export setups this project holds - DWG/DXF, DGN, PDF and print - and the options in each.

Answers which export setups the project holds and what is in each - the DWG/DXF export setups, the DGN export setups, the PDF export setups (Revit 2022 and later) and the print settings - each by name, which one is active, and its key options in the export dialog's words: file version, units, coordinate basis, how views on sheets are exported, layer standard, solids, colours, line scaling, and for PDF the paper, zoom, colour and file naming. A question, read and never changed; it opens no transaction. **ONE SETUP NAMED SHOWS ITS LAYER TABLE.** With a setup's name given, its category-to-layer rows are listed as well. **IFC, NAVISWORKS, DWF AND IMAGE EXPORT ARE NOT LISTED.** They keep no saved setup the Revit API can read, and the answer says so.

<a id="manage-export-setups"></a>

### Manage export setups

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** create, copy, rename or delete a DWG, DGN, PDF or print export setup by name.

Creates, copies, renames or deletes a saved export setup by name - the DWG/DXF export setups, the DGN export setups, the PDF export setups (Revit 2022 and later) and the print settings. Copying keeps every option of the setup it starts from under the new name. **A NAME THAT IS NOT THERE IS REFUSED, NAMING IT AND THE ONES THAT ARE.** So is a new name already in use for that kind, and a name found under two kinds when the kind was not said. **DELETING A SETUP IS DESTRUCTIVE.** It is asked for by name, one setup at a time, and needs the modeller's yes for that setup first (Article 7). **PRINT SETTINGS GO THROUGH THE PRINT MANAGER**, which is application state and not undone by Undo, so the current print setting is put back afterwards and the reply says which it is. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

| **You get** | done, kind used, now called, setups now |

<a id="set-export-setup-options"></a>

### Set export setup options

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** change the options saved in a DWG, DXF, DGN or PDF export setup - version, units, coordinates, layers.

Changes named options of one saved export setup - a DWG/DXF, DGN or PDF (Revit 2022 and later) export setup - and keeps its name: the file version, export units, coordinate basis (shared or project internal), solids, colours, line scaling, whether views on sheets are exported as external references, the layer standard, the hide options, one category's layer name in the layer table, and for PDF the paper, orientation, zoom, colour, quality and whether files are combined. Every option is read back afterwards. **ALL OR NOTHING.** An option it does not know, or a value that option does not take, refuses the whole call, naming what it does take, and the setup is left exactly as it was. **A SETUP NAME THAT IS NOT THERE IS REFUSED, NAMING IT AND THE ONES THAT ARE.** ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).
